concepts.learning_objective: State the precise definition of a quadrilateral and recognise figures it excludes.
Identify vertices, sides, diagonals, adjacent and opposite parts, and valid names of a quadrilateral.
Decide whether a quadrilateral is convex using its internal angles or its diagonals.
Recognise non-convex, self-intersecting and non-planar 4-gons and where they arise.
Recall and justify the side, angle and diagonal properties of a parallelogram.
Use the converse tests and the equal parallel sides test to show a quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

topics.title: The Midpoint Theorem and its Converse

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the Midpoint Theorem to find lengths and parallel segments in a triangle.
Apply the converse of the Midpoint Theorem to locate midpoints.
Use the concurrence of medians and the 2 : 1 division at the centroid.
Show that the midpoints of the sides of any quadrilateral form a parallelogram and relate it to the diagonals.
Explain how copies of any quadrilateral can tile the plane.
Use the 360 degree angle condition at a vertex to decide whether a shape can tile.
